name: Meloxicam
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Meloxicam is an oxicam nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) cleared by liver metabolism. The US label needs no dose change in mild to moderate kidney impairment, does not recommend it in severe impairment, and caps the dose at 7.5 mg/day in hemodialysis; it is not dialyzable. NSAID kidney risks (acute kidney injury, hyperkalemia, fluid retention) still apply.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses qualitative grades (mild, moderate, severe renal impairment). Mapping 'severe' to CrCl <30 is our judgment.

bands.recommendation: 7.5 mg once daily; may increase to 15 mg once daily; maximum 15 mg/day (label).
No dose adjustment in mild to moderate impairment (label 8.7). Monitor creatinine, potassium and blood pressure; avoid volume depletion and the ACE inhibitor or ARB plus diuretic combination.
bands.short: No dose change; monitor SCr, K, BP

bands.recommendation: Severe renal impairment: not studied and not recommended (label 2.5, 8.7). Avoid in advanced kidney disease unless benefits outweigh the risk (label 5.6).
Severe renal impairment: not studied and not recommended (label 2.5, 8.7). Avoid in advanced kidney disease unless benefits outweigh the risk (label 5.6).

hd.text: Maximum 7.5 mg/day (label 2.1, 8.7). Not dialyzable, so no supplement. NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

pd.text: Not studied. Label: severe renal impairment not recommended; the 7.5 mg/day cap is for hemodialysis only. Applying the cap to PD would be clinical extrapolation. Specialist input.
pd.short: Not studied; severe CKD not advised

crrt.text: Avoid: NSAIDs can worsen acute kidney injury.

dialyzable: No: meloxicam is not dialyzable (label 8.7); about 99.4% protein-bound.
monitoring: Creatinine, potassium and blood pressure in CKD, heart failure, liver disease, dehydration or with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or diuretics (label 5.6). Edema; hemoglobin if anemia symptoms.

pediatric.approved_ages: Juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (JRA), weight 60 kg or more (label); studied from 2 to 17 years.
pediatric.usual_dose: 7.5 mg once daily if weight 60 kg or more; do not use under 60 kg (tablets; label).
pediatric.max_dose: 7.5 mg once daily (no added benefit above 7.5 mg in trials).

renal.recommendation: 7.5 mg once daily if 60 kg or more (label).
No pediatric kidney data; adult label: no adjustment in mild to moderate impairment. Monitor creatinine and potassium.
renal.short: No dose data; monitor SCr, K

renal.recommendation: Not recommended in severe renal impairment (label statement not limited by age).
Not recommended in severe renal impairment.

hd.text: Not studied in children on dialysis; no pediatric dose.

sources.citation: Redpharm Drug. (2026). Meloxicam tablets [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, ANDA077921, set ID 58d34e5d-4efb-3d76-e063-6394a90aa0f6, version effective October 2, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

adult: Selected label is a generic tablet ANDA (Redpharm); its text includes 'not interchangeable with other formulations', copied from the reference product.
PH strengths 7.5 and 15 mg match US; one PH 10 mg product has no US equivalent.
PD tile red by extrapolation from 'severe impairment not recommended'; label HD cap could be argued for PD (judgment).
